question.leadin: One noblewoman from this family was blamed for instigating a massacre of thousands of Huguenots in France on St. Bartholomew's Day.
question.text: Name this European family to which Catherine, the wife of King Henry II, belonged. Cosimo established this family's dominance over the city of Florence during the Renaissance.
question.answerHtml: Medici [MEH-dih-chee] family (accept Catherine de’ Medici or Cosimo de’ Medici )
question.clue: People with this last name founded a Platonic Academy and were targeted in the Pazzi Conspiracy.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the newspaper Avanti!
swap.text: Although he had formerly edited it, this fascist leader banned the publication of Avanti! when he took power. Nicknamed "Il Duce", he led the Blackshirts during the March on Rome.
swap.clue: Futurist artists glorified this leader, who began the Pacification of Libya.

question.leadin: This bearded warrior led the Expedition of the Thousand while conquering the Kingdom of Two Sicilies for King Victor Emmanuel II.
question.text: Name this leader of the Red Shirts during Italian unification.
question.clue: This man led a small force to victory with an uphill bayonet charge at Calatafimi shortly before declaring himself dictator of Sicily.

swap.leadin: This man created the Rome-Berlin Axis with Adolf Hitler.
swap.text: Name this fascist dictator of Italy known as Il Duce, or "the Boss," who took power after a March on Rome.
swap.clue: He later ran Il Popolo D'Italia and nurtured a grudge against the Socialists for expelling him.

question.text: The refusal of Henry the Lion to help Frederick at the Battle of Legnano led to his defeat against this organization. This organization signed the Peace of Constance with Frederick.
question.clue: The successes of this organization include forcing the Peace of Constance, after which this group dissolved for a time, though it was later defeated at the Battle of Cortenuova after reforming.

swap.leadin: The Black Death may have first arrived in Europe during the Golden Horde's siege of this city's colony of Caffa.
swap.text: Name this Italian city. This maritime republic was the home city of Christopher Columbus.
swap.clue: A territory ruled by this city was attacked in 1553 by a joint Franco-Ottoman force under Turgut Reis.

question.leadin: Troops occupying this city were ordered to smoke large cigars in the street after its residents boycotted tobacco.
question.text: Name this city that forced out its Austrian garrison during the "Five Days" in 1848. Before passing to the control of the Habsburgs, this city was ruled by the Sforza family.
question.clue: Its history of family rule began with the Torrianis, who were soon rivaled by the Viscontis.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about slaves in the ancient world.
swap.text: Due to the mistreatment of slaves on this island, three Servile Wars were fought. Spartacus began his slave revolt on this island.
swap.clue: A civil war in this place ended via the Treaty of Caltabellota, while Muslim rule of this place ended with the invasion of a man who would fight Alexius Comnenus at Dyrrhachium and had Bohemund as his son.

question.text: This Genoese admiral and "perpetual censor" made his fame in a later Italian War by liberating Marseilles for the French. His nephew of the same last name led a fleet at Lepanto, and a ship named for him collided with the MS Stockholm in 1956.
question.clue: This man was made Prince of Melfi by Holy Roman Emperor Charles V after betraying Francis I during the Siege of Naples.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Romulus Augustulus, the final emperor of the Western Roman Empire.
swap.text: From 402 until the collapse of the Roman Empire, this city served as its capital. In later times, this city was the seat of the Kingdom of Lombardy.
swap.clue: It became the seat of the Byzantine governor of Italy in the sixth century, and its namesake Cosmography was written around 700.

question.text: This son of Rodrigo Borgia was made a cardinal by his father in 1493. Machiavelli thought highly of him, but he died in a minor battle in at the age of 31.
question.clue: This man was the illegitimate son of the notorious Pope Alexander VI, and some scholarship selects this man as the assassin of his brother Giovanni, who died under mysterious circumstances.

swap.text: Pepin helped the papacy against this Germanic ethnic group, which had spread across Italy. This ethnic group, whose "Iron Crown" was used to crown Italian rulers, gives its name to a modern-day region in northern Italy.
swap.clue: The death of that king, Liutprand, is the final event in a history of these peoples written by Paul the Deacon.

question.text: While in power, Mussolini was known by this title bestowed upon him by the Grand Council of Fascism. It can be translated to mean "leader" in Italian.
question.clue: This two word term means "leader" in Italian and was the title used by Mussolini during part of his reign.

swap.leadin: In his Autobiography, Benvenuto Cellini claimed to have killed Charles of Bourbon during this event.
swap.text: Name this 1527 event that began after Francis I joined the League of Cognac ("KON-yak"). During this event, Caspar Roist led the Swiss Guard in its "last stand," allowing an escape to the Castel Sant'Angelo.
swap.answerHtml: 1527 Sack of Rome [do not accept or prompt on “French Sack of Rome”]
swap.clue: The leader targeted by this event started a fashion for long beards by not shaving in mourning over this event, which he was able to escape via a secret passage thanks to the suicidal stand of Kaspar Roist's troops.

question.text: al-Idrisi is best known for a south-up map created for a ruler with this name, whose coronation mantle features two lines and the Islamic date 528. This first King of Sicily's Hauteville Dynasty had this name.
question.clue: This name of a king of Sicily, whose father of the same name was the brother of Robert Guiscard ("ro-BEHR ghis-CAR"). That king of this name commissioned a namesake world map, created by Muhammad al-Idrisi at his court in 1138.

swap.leadin: One of this party's early leaders claimed his approach was influenced by Benedetto Croce.
swap.text: Name this Italian political party founded by Antonio Gramsci and once led by Palmiro Togliatti. It entered a "historic compromise" with its country's Christian Democrats in the 1970s.
swap.clue: This organization joined the CLN on the eve of World War II as part of a strategy known as the Salerno turn.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about Italian politics during the First World War.
question.text: This man headed the Italian delegation to the Paris Peace Conference to round out the "Big Four." He served as prime minister of Italy from 1917 to 1919.
question.clue: This leader who upset nationalists by failing to address the broken London Pact.

swap.text: After the Bajamonte Tiepolo against the Doge in 1310, this secretive council was created, named for the original number of its members, and given emergency powers in Venice. It was led by men called Capi who were confined to live in the Doge's Palace.
swap.clue: Prior to becoming doge, Faliero served in this body that secretly monitored the activities of all Venetians. Citizens could submit information to this body by placing letters in bocche di leone ("BOKE-kay dee lay-OH-nay").

question.leadin: How much do you really know about the Treaty of Utrecht? Answer, FTPE.
question.text: This Italian state and ally of England received Sicily.
question.clue: This region. Conrad the Salic made Humbert the Whitehanded the first count of this region after he crushed an uprising in Saint-Jean-de-Maurienne ("sen-zhahn-duh-mor-YEN").

swap.leadin: King Charles Robert I of this dynasty appears on the 200 Forint bill in Hungary, which he ruled from 1312 to 1342.
swap.text: Name this royal house from the namesake area of France, who descend from a younger son of Blanche of Castile and more notably ruled Sicily and Naples.
swap.clue: In 1460, Skanderbeg led an expedition to help Ferdinand I of Naples defend against this house. A member of this house, Charles II, defended against the House of Barcelona in the War of the Sicilian Vespers.
